subject: VMWARE_ESXI

sutProfile.guestDriver: virtio-net plus raw PCI config and Linux AER counter probe
sutProfile.workload: Correctable-only Receiver Error across all E/M/R gates in PassthruIdle, active g100/g101 representatives, and QEMU eight-bit by eight-gate positive control

inputs.gateTuple: G=(Endpoint CERE, selected Correctable Mask bit, Root COR_EN)

expected: Endpoint status deposition, fabric Root deposition, Root notification eligibility, guest capability visibility, raw status projection and guest/host service events are evaluated as separate outcomes.
The QEMU public-model positive control distinguishes all eight Correctable bits across all eight E/M/R tuples without any Uncorrectable side effect.
Every ESXi case uses a requested-bit-clean strict baseline, restores the original gate and Root-path state, and stops if an Uncorrectable surface changes.
A bounded absence of guest or host log events is reported as a negative observation rather than proof of no ESXi service.
observed: QEMU 11.0.2 passed 64 of 64 Correctable-bit by E/M/R rows: every row deposited the requested Endpoint CES/CED bit, while only E=1,M=0 rows g100 and g101 recorded Root COR_RCV.
ESXi PassthruIdle Receiver Error passed all eight E/M/R rows; only g100 and g101 had frozen outer-QEMU Root reception, and every row restored the original gate without an Uncorrectable delta.
Active g100 and g101 each passed a Correctable-only injection with stable VM ownership, a responsive host, frozen Root reception and no Uncorrectable side effect.

The virtio guest exposed AER header 0x00020001 and raw CES changed from 0x00000000 to 0x00000001, while TOTAL_ERR_COR, TOTAL_ERR_FATAL and TOTAL_ERR_NONFATAL remained zero and no semantic Linux AER event line appeared.

After collection-path and command noise was excluded, no semantic AER or PCI error event appeared in the bounded ESXi host log windows; this does not identify or exclude an internal ESXi interrupt or service path.

The tested e1000e and virtio profiles expose different guest AER capability surfaces, so capability visibility, raw status projection and service/event delivery are independent versioned policy dimensions.
limitations: The frozen Root observations prove outer-QEMU fabric deposition while ESXi execution is paused; they do not attribute an ESXi interrupt, Root service or private implementation path.
The aggregate active-v2 result is INCONCLUSIVE because its g101 row did not inject; only its g100 subcase is behavior evidence, and the separate final g101 run supplies the R=1 observation.
The active-v2 guest and host event classifications contained parser false positives; canonical event conclusions use raw-log reclassification plus the corrected final live smoke.
Active g100 and g101 are single successful observations and do not meet the planned three-run repeatability requirement.
Guest writes, Root W1C repeat/re-arm behavior, lifecycle clear/reuse and physical reset/health/quarantine are not tested.
Synthetic AER injection does not reproduce electrical link errors or physical device internal state.
The raw run directories are external sibling artifacts and are not committed to this repository; their exact result and manifest hashes are pinned in the registered summary.
The observation is limited to one nested q35/OVMF ESXi build, one synthetic virtio endpoint and one EFI Linux guest; it is not Qman product conformance or physical qualification.
